text.p: Swedish chemicals company Perstorp on Tuesday said it expected its results in 1996/97 to be about the same as in the previous year.

"There are signs that the economic downturn in Europe will bottom out during the end of 1996 and that an upturn will come about in 1997," the company's chief executive officer Gosta Wiking said in a statement.

"Investments in combination with increased development and research and other investments will, however, have a significant impact on earnings during the first half of the reporting year (from September 1996 to February 1998)."
"Uncertainty about economic trends makes it hard to adjust full-year earnings, but we expect to reach earnings of the same size as last reporting year."
In the year from September 1995 to the end of August 1996, Perstorp reported a pre-tax profit of 716 million crowns against 745 million crowns in the previous year.
